title: Authorization & Token Flow
description: Implement the authorization endpoint (login page with username/password form) and token endpoint (exchanges auth code for JWT). This is the core OIDC authentication flow.

title: Authorization endpoint with login page (GET /auth)
description: Implement GET /auth endpoint. This is the authorization endpoint in the OIDC flow. It must: 1) Accept query params: client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope, state. 2) Render a minimal HTML login form with username and password fields and a Login button. 3) On form submission (POST /auth), validate username/password against the configured users. 4) On success, generate a random authorization code, store it in memory (mapped to the authenticated user and redirect_uri), and redirect to redirect_uri?code={code}&state={state}. 5) On failure, re-render the login page with an error message. Auth codes should expire after a short TTL (e.g. 5 minutes).

title: Token endpoint (POST /token)
description: Implement POST /token endpoint. Accepts form-encoded body with: grant_type=authorization_code, code (the auth code from /auth), redirect_uri, client_id. Must: 1) Validate the auth code exists, hasn't expired, and redirect_uri matches. 2) Consume the auth code (one-time use). 3) Generate a signed JWT ID token with claims: iss (ISSUER_URL), sub (username), aud (client_id), exp, iat, email, name. Sign with RS256 using the in-memory private key. Include kid in JWT header. 4) Return JSON response: {access_token, token_type: bearer, id_token, expires_in}. The access_token can be the same as the id_token for simplicity.

title: OIDC Discovery & Cryptographic Keys
description: Implement in-memory RSA key generation, JWKS endpoint, and OIDC discovery document. These are the foundational OIDC endpoints that the enterprise product queries to learn about the IdP.

title: In-memory RSA key pair generation
description: Generate an RSA key pair (2048-bit) on startup. Store in memory only. The private key is used for signing JWTs, the public key is exposed via JWKS. Generate a stable key ID (kid) for the key. Use crypto/rsa and crypto/rand from stdlib. Key is regenerated each time the process starts (no persistence).

title: JWKS endpoint (GET /jwks)
description: Implement GET /jwks endpoint that returns the public key in JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) format. Must include: kty=RSA, use=sig, alg=RS256, kid (matching the key ID used in JWT headers), n (modulus, base64url), e (exponent, base64url). Response Content-Type: application/json.

title: OIDC Discovery endpoint (GET /.well-known/openid-configuration)
description: Implement GET /.well-known/openid-configuration returning a JSON discovery document. Required fields: issuer (ISSUER_URL), authorization_endpoint ({ISSUER_URL}/auth), token_endpoint ({ISSUER_URL}/token), jwks_uri ({ISSUER_URL}/jwks), response_types_supported ([code]), subject_types_supported ([public]), id_token_signing_alg_values_supported ([RS256]), scopes_supported ([openid, email, profile]), grant_types_supported ([authorization_code]). Content-Type: application/json.

title: Project Scaffolding & Configuration
description: Set up Go module, HTTP server, routing, and environment variable configuration. Structure the code to support future SCIM extensibility.

title: Initialize Go module and project structure
description: Run go mod init, create main.go entry point, and establish the package structure. Packages should be organized to allow SCIM to be added later as a separate package. Suggested structure: main.go (entry point, server setup), internal/config/ (env var parsing), internal/oidc/ (OIDC endpoints and logic), internal/crypto/ (key generation and JWT). No third-party dependencies.

title: Implement HTTP server with routing
description: Set up net/http server with a mux that routes to the four OIDC endpoints: GET /.well-known/openid-configuration, GET /jwks, GET /auth, POST /token. Server should listen on a configurable port (env var). Use standard library only.

title: Environment variable configuration
description: Parse all configuration from environment variables. Required vars: ISSUER_URL (the external URL of this IdP, used in discovery doc and JWT issuer claim), PORT (listen port, default 8080), CLIENT_ID (the client ID that the enterprise product will use). All state in RAM only, no disk artifacts.

title: User configuration via environment variables
description: Support multiple users configured via environment variable. Suggested format: USERS env var containing JSON array, e.g. [{"username":"alice","password":"pass123","email":"alice@example.com","name":"Alice Smith"}]. Each user needs: username (for login), password (for login), email (JWT claim), name/display name (JWT claim). The sub claim in the JWT can be derived from username. All user data lives in RAM only.

title: Unit Tests
description: Comprehensive unit tests for all OIDC components. Integration testing will be done manually by the user against the enterprise product.

title: Unit tests for crypto and JWT generation
description: Test RSA key generation (valid key, correct size), JWKS serialization (valid JSON, correct fields, base64url encoding), and JWT generation (valid signature, correct claims, correct header with kid and alg).

title: Unit tests for discovery and JWKS endpoints
description: Test that GET /.well-known/openid-configuration returns valid JSON with all required fields and correct URLs. Test that GET /jwks returns valid JWKS with the public key. Use httptest for handler testing.

title: Unit tests for authorization and token flow
description: Test the full auth code flow: 1) GET /auth renders login form. 2) POST /auth with valid credentials redirects with code and state. 3) POST /auth with invalid credentials shows error. 4) POST /token with valid code returns JWT. 5) POST /token with expired/invalid code returns error. 6) Auth code is single-use. Use httptest for handler testing.
